trust_decision.summary: Whether a LaTeX command that can load resources or set HTML attributes (\href, \url, \includegraphics, \htmlClass/\htmlId/\htmlStyle/\htmlData) is allowed is decided by Settings.isTrusted from the resolved this.trust, which is filled per-option by applySetting/getDefaultValue from the caller's options object and the SETTINGS_SCHEMA entry; the fix makes each of those lookups own-property-only so a value inherited from a polluted prototype cannot become the decision input.

landing_point.why: The summary says settings/trust prototype pollution, so a reader starts at the options-to-Settings copy: `options[prop]` walks the prototype chain, so a polluted Object.prototype.trust becomes an own `this.trust` on the Settings instance and isTrusted then returns true.

fix_sites.entry_point: katex.render, katex.renderToString, katex.__parse, katex.__renderToDomTree, katex.__renderToHTMLTree and the `katex` CLI bin, all through new Settings(options)
same set: katex.render, renderToString, __parse, __renderToDomTree, __renderToHTMLTree, CLI (new Settings(options))
katex.render / renderToString macro expansion: MacroExpander._getExpansion -> Namespace.get, with builtins = src/macros.ts map and current = settings.macros
\def / \newcommand / \gdef in the input, and Parser.ts:131 macros.set("\\color", ...) when colorIsTextColor is set
fix_sites.module_kind: library core (macro namespace group undo stack)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Namespace is the macro/undo-stack class, has no trust decision of its own, already used hasOwnProperty on `current` in get()/has(), and the advisory is titled 'settings' prototype pollution with Settings.trust as the reported sink - so a solver can fix Settings.ts only and call the macro namespace a separate, already-guarded concern.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: trust and strict are legitimately boolean-or-function (and strict may also be 'warn'|'ignore'|'error'); an over-broad hardening that coerces or validates option values (Boolean(optionValue), requiring a boolean trust) breaks the documented function forms that the existing trust tests rely on, because isTrusted calls this.trust(context).

O6_input_shapes: plain object literal with own keys
options object whose prototype carries the key (Object.create({trust: true}), Settings.ts:376-378)
globally polluted Object.prototype keys (trust, default, processor)
own property explicitly set to undefined, which must fall back to the default
schema entry with no own `default` or `processor` (implicit default, enum[0])
macro map passed as settings.macros, and the builtin macro map, with names only on the prototype chain
function-valued options (trust, strict) passed through unchanged

O7_producer.where: src/Settings.ts:197-297 (SETTINGS_SCHEMA), consumed by the constructor loop at src/Settings.ts:379-385

O8_uncovered_routes.route: isTrusted derives the protocol with `"url" in context` and a plain read of `context.protocol`; a polluted Object.prototype.protocol (e.g. 'http') makes `!context.protocol` false, skips protocolFromUrl, and hands the documented trust functions a forged protocol, so trust: (c) => c.protocol === 'http' approves \href{javascript:...}. The fix has no hunk here.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: isTrusted is the check itself, so it looks already correct; the fix's new tests only pollute trust/default/processor and only construct new Settings(), never pollute protocol, so a solver who reproduces the reported shape sees nothing left to change there.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, 0 files away

O8_uncovered_routes.route: cli.js reads schema metadata with plain property reads (opt.cli !== false, opt.cli || ..., opt.cliDescription, opt.cliProcessor, opt.cliDefault) and passes them to commander, so a polluted Object.prototype.cliDefault becomes an own default for every flag - including --trust - which then reaches Settings as an own option property and is accepted by the patched hasOwnProperty(options, prop) check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: cli.js is a Node convenience binary outside src/, not the library rendering path the advisory describes, and prototype pollution in a short-lived CLI process looks unreachable to most solvers.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: repo root, 1 file outside src/, reached only through the `katex` bin (package.json bin, cli.js:93)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: contrib/auto-render merges caller options onto a fresh object and then reads defaults off the prototype chain (`optionsCopy.macros || {}`, delimiters, ignoredClasses, errorCallback), re-materialising a polluted Object.prototype.macros as an own optionsCopy.macros that the patched Settings own-property check must accept, injecting macro definitions into the Namespace.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is a separate contrib package entry (katex/contrib/auto-render) that only decides which macros exist, not trust itself, so it reads as a neighbouring feature outside the advisory's settings path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate package entry contrib/auto-render, 1 package away from src/

O8b_injection_room.sibling: one more HTML-attribute command (e.g. \htmlTooltip or \dataAttr) building a trust context, with its own isTrusted-style helper that indexes a plain config/trust map
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the html.ts handler already switches per command and builds a context object each time; copying that shape for a new attribute command is the obvious extension, and a helper indexing a plain object would reintroduce inherited reads.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second Namespace instance for grouped counters/registers (\newcount, \setcounter) built from a caller-supplied map
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Namespace is generic over Value and its constructor takes any user map, so a maintainer adding grouped, undo-stack-restored state would reuse it with state that came from options.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new merged option added the same way as macros/ignoredClasses (default read off optionsCopy, then assigned as own)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every existing default in this function uses `optionsCopy.x || <default>`, so a new option naturally inherits the same re-materialisation of a polluted prototype value.

O9_family: CWE-807 reliance on an untrusted input in a security decision, reached through prototype pollution (own-property vs prototype-chain lookups of settings, schema metadata and macro names)
